Note the ambiguity check still precedes it: `--payload '--=x y' --secret s` -> exit 2 `ambiguous option: --=x y could match --help, --payload, --secret`.

verdicts.rule: classify step 6a (LONG ABBREVIATION): unique prefix match -> OPTION. `--pay`/`--p` -> --payload; `--sec`/`--s` -> --secret.
verdicts.note: `--p a --s s` -> exit 0 `{'data': 'a'}`. Extra: `--s x --p y` -> exit 0 `{'data': 'y'}`; `--se x --pa y` -> exit 0 `{'data': 'y'}`; `--h`, `--he`, `--hel` all -> help, exit 0.

verdicts.rule: classify step 6a with explicit arg: `--pay=a --sec=s` works; abbreviations classified as OPTION cannot be values.
verdicts.note: `--pay=a --sec=s` -> exit 0 `{'data': 'a'}`. `--payload '--pay=1' --secret s` -> exit 2 `argument --payload: expected one argument`. Also `--payload '--se' --secret s` -> exit 2 same. Note the abbreviated form of --help with '=' errors: `--h=1` -> exit 2 `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1'`.

verdicts.rule: classify step 6 AMBIGUITY: >1 candidate -> "ambiguous option: <tok> could match <o1>, <o2>, ..." in registration order, exit 2 immediately.
verdicts.note: `--=x` , `--=` , `--=x=` , `--=x y` all -> exit 2, e.g. `test8_executable: error: ambiguous option: --= could match --help, --payload, --secret`. Worth recording for a reimplementation: with this option set only 3-candidate ambiguities are reachable (the only shared prefix is `--`), and `-h` is never listed because it does not start with `--`.

verdicts.rule: classify step 6b (SHORT CONCATENATION, before negative-number and space rules): tok[0]=='-', tok[1]!='-'; if tok.slice(0,2) is a known option -> OPTION with explicitArg=tok.slice(2). Any token matching /^-h/ is an OPTION even with spaces.
verdicts.note: `--payload '-h x' --secret s` -> exit 2 `argument --payload: expected one argument`; `--payload '-h ' --secret s` -> exit 2 same; `--payload '-hx' --secret s` -> exit 2 same. Corollary the rules never state explicitly: a bare `'-h '` (trailing space) as argv[1] prints help and exits 0 — the space rule is genuinely unreachable for /^-h/ tokens.

verdicts.rule: classify step 6b negative case: single-dash tokens whose first two chars are not '-h' get no match; '-p' does not abbreviate --payload; falls through to unknown OPTION.
verdicts.note: `--payload '-p' --secret s` -> exit 2 `argument --payload: expected one argument`; same for `-x`, `-=x`, `-x=y`.

verdicts.rule: classify step 7 (NEGATIVE NUMBER): /^-\d+$/u or /^-\d*\.\d+$/u with Unicode Nd -> VALUE.
verdicts.note: Reproduced their whole list and extended it. Accepted (exit 0, VALUE): -1, -1.5, -.5, -01, -0.0, -0, -000.000, -.0, -١ (U+0661), -١٢٣, -１ (U+FF11), -٠.٥, -1٢3 (mixed scripts!), -๓ (U+0E53 Thai), -𝟙 (U+1D7D9, astral Nd). Rejected (exit 2 `argument --payload: expected one argument`): -1., -., -..5, -1e5, -1.5e3, -1.0.0, -1_0, -1,5, -1-1, -1x, --1, --1.5, -➊ (U+278A, No). Their table's row for `-.` is garbled (shows `{'data': '- '}`) but the classification stated (rejected) is what I measured for the exact token `-.`. Note for JS: astral Nd like U+1D7D9 means you must use /\p{Nd}/u, and the token is one code point, so a code-unit-based regex without /u will also fail.

verdicts.rule: classify step 8 (SPACE RULE): only U+0020 anywhere -> VALUE; TAB/NEWLINE do not count.
verdicts.note: Reproduced, and widened the whitespace set — ONLY U+0020 works. All of these -> exit 2 `argument --payload: expected one argument`: `-\tx` (U+0009), `-x\n` (U+000A), `-x\vy` (U+000B), `-x y` (NBSP), `-x　y` (ideographic space). All of these -> exit 0: `' '`, `'- '`, `' -x'`, `'-x '`, `'-x y'`, `'--x y'`, `'-- x'`, `'-- '`, `'- 1'`. Caveat a reimplementer must keep: because this is step 8, a space does NOT rescue a token that already matched at steps 3/5/6 — `'--=x y'` -> ambiguous error, `'--p=x y'` and `'-h x'` -> OPTION.

verdicts.rule: classify step 9 (FALLTHROUGH): anything else starting with '-' -> unknown OPTION; never usable as a value.
verdicts.note: `--payload -x --secret s` -> exit 2 `argument --payload: expected one argument`. Standalone `--x` -> exit 2 `the following arguments are required: --payload, --secret` (unknown option consumed into extras, required check wins). `--bogus=1` behaves the same way (whole token, '=' and all, goes to extras).

verdicts.rule: PHASE 2 (consume): zero positionals; walk to maxOptIdx, flushing intervening tokens into `extras` in order, then append the tail.
verdicts.note: `x --payload a y --secret s z` -> exit 2 `unrecognized arguments: x y z`. New cases: `--payload a b --secret s` -> `unrecognized arguments: b`; `--payload a --secret s b -- c` -> `unrecognized arguments: b -- c` (tail after the last option, marker included verbatim); `--bogus x --payload a --secret s`-style ordering holds too (`--payload a --secret s --bogus -- z` -> `unrecognized arguments: --bogus -- z`).

verdicts.rule: PHASE 2 consuming a 1-arg option without explicitArg: takes tokens[next+1] only if it exists and is VALUE; else "argument <NAME>: expected one argument" with NAME = registered option_strings, never the typed abbreviation.
verdicts.note: `--pay` -> `argument --payload: expected one argument`; `--p=1 --s` -> `argument --secret: expected one argument`; `--payload --secret` -> `argument --payload: ...` (leftmost option errors first); `--secret --payload a` -> `argument --secret: ...`; `--payload a --secret` (EOF) -> `argument --secret: ...`. All exit 2.

verdicts.rule: KEY `--` RULE A: the MARKER blocks the immediately-preceding option from taking a value.
verdicts.note: All exit 2 with `argument --payload: expected one argument`: `--payload -- --secret s`, `--payload -- --`, `--payload -- --secret=s`, `--payload -- -h`, `--payload -h -- x`, `--pay -- a` (abbreviation form, name still reported as --payload). `--secret -- --payload a` -> `argument --secret: expected one argument`.

verdicts.rule: KEY `--` RULE B: the MARKER is not swallowed; with no positionals it appears verbatim in extras / "unrecognized arguments".
verdicts.note: Exit 2 for all: `--payload a --secret s --` -> `unrecognized arguments: --`; `... -- x` -> `-- x`; `... -- -- x` -> `-- -- x`; `... -- x --` -> `-- x --`; `... -- -h` -> `-- -h`; `--payload=a --secret=s --` -> `unrecognized arguments: --`.

verdicts.rule: KEY `--` RULE C: options after the marker are inert, so requiredness is not satisfied.
verdicts.note: `--payload a -- --secret s` -> `the following arguments are required: --secret`; `-- --payload a --secret s` and `-- --payload=a --secret=s` and `--` and `-- -h` -> `--payload, --secret`; `--secret s -- --payload a` -> `--payload`; `--payload=a -- --secret=s` -> `--secret`. New: `--bogus -- -h` -> `the following arguments are required: --payload, --secret` (the post-marker -h does not fire help). All exit 2.

verdicts.rule: KEY `--` RULE D: `--` attached via '=' is not a marker; `--`-looking tokens with a space are plain VALUEs.
verdicts.note: `--payload=-- --secret s` -> exit 0 `{'data': '--'}`. `--payload '-- ' --secret s`, `--payload ' --' --secret s`, `--payload '-- x' --secret s` all exit 0 with the raw string.

verdicts.rule: KEY `--` RULE E (multi `--`): only the first is the marker; later ones are ordinary VALUEs and appear verbatim in extras in order.
verdicts.note: `--payload a --secret s -- -- --` -> exit 2 `unrecognized arguments: -- -- --`; `--payload a --secret s -- --` -> `-- --`.

verdicts.rule: ERROR PRECEDENCE strict order: (1) scan ambiguous; (2) help; (3) ignored-explicit / expected-one-argument; (4) required; (5) unrecognized.
verdicts.note: Levels (2) and (3) are NOT ranked — they are resolved strictly by position in the phase-2 left-to-right walk, so a consume error at an earlier index beats a later help. Counterexample: `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable --payload -h` -> EXIT=2, stdout empty, stderr `test8_executable: error: argument --payload: expected one argument`. The stated order predicts help/exit 0. Same for `--payload -h -h`, `--payload -h -- x`, `--payload --pay=1`. Symmetrically `--help=1 -h` -> EXIT=2 `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '1'` while `-h -h=x` -> EXIT=0 help. Corrected precedence: (1) scan-phase ambiguous-option error (whole argv, beats everything, incl. `-h=x --=y` -> ambiguous); (2) the FIRST event encountered walking phase-2 options left to right, whichever it is — help action (print help to stdout, exit 0) or an `ignored explicit argument` / `expected one argument` error (exit 2); (3) `the following arguments are required: ...`; (4) `unrecognized arguments: ...`. Levels (3)/(4) verified ordered: `--payload a -- x` -> `the following arguments are required: --secret` even though extras are non-empty.

verdicts.rule: REQUIRED-ARGS message: "the following arguments are required: " + missing.join(', ') in registration order; exit 2.
verdicts.note: Bare invocation -> `test8_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --payload, --secret`, exit 2. `--secret s -- --payload a` -> `--payload`; `--payload a -- --secret s` -> `--secret`.

verdicts.rule: UNRECOGNIZED message: "unrecognized arguments: " + extras.join(' ') with raw token text; empty-string extras produce visible extra spaces.
verdicts.note: `--payload a --secret s '' -- ''` -> `unrecognized arguments:  -- $` (cat -A). Extended: `--payload a --secret s '' '' ''` -> `unrecognized arguments:   $` (three empty extras = colon+space then two joining spaces); `--payload a --secret s ' '` -> `unrecognized arguments:  $`; `--payload a --secret s ''` -> `unrecognized arguments: $` (trailing space after the colon, nothing else).

verdicts.rule: REPEATED options: last occurrence wins.
verdicts.note: `--payload a --payload b --secret s` -> exit 0 `{'data': 'b'}`. Also works across forms: `--p=1 --payload z --secret s` style; `--payload --payload a --secret s` is instead an error (`argument --payload: expected one argument`) because the second `--payload` is an OPTION, not a value.

verdicts.rule: EXPLICIT-ARG on the 0-arg help action: `-h<tail>` -> help unless the split was on '=' or tail starts with '-', in which case "argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument '<tail>'".
verdicts.note: Mispredicts any tail that begins with one or more extra 'h' characters, because argparse re-enters the single-dash unpacking loop and re-splits the remaining tail. Counterexamples (all exit 2, stdout empty): `/workspace/dataset/test8_executable -hh=x` -> `test8_executable: error: argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` (rule predicts help, since tail `h=x` does not start with '-' and the top-level split was not on '='); `-hhh=x` -> same, `'x'`; `-hh=` -> `ignored explicit argument ''`; `-hh-x` -> `ignored explicit argument '-x'` (rule predicts help). Meanwhile these DO print help, exit 0: `-hx=y`, `-h0=1`, `-hh1=2`, `-hhx=y`, `-hh`, `-hhh`, `-hhx`, `-hxh=y`, `-hha`, `-hfoo`, `-h1`, `-h `. Correct mechanical rule (single-dash peel loop), for opt='-h', sep and expl from classification: loop { if expl===null -> run help, exit 0; if expl==='' -> error `ignored explicit argument ''`; if sep==='=' || expl[0]==='-' -> error `ignored explicit argument '<expl>'`; if ('-'+expl[0]) is not a known option ('-h' is the only one) -> run help, exit 0; else expl=expl.slice(1); if expl==='' {expl=null; sep=null} else if (expl[0]==='=') {sep='='; expl=expl.slice(1)} else {sep=''} }. The reference JS in the notes implements only one pass and therefore prints help for `-hh=x` / `-hh-x`. Confirmed unchanged: `-h=`, `-h=x`, `-h-x`, `-h--`, `-h-1`, `--help=1`, `--help=`, `--h=1` -> error; error text always names the action `-h/--help`.

verdicts.rule: OPTION=VALUE always bypasses classification of the value (`--payload=-x`, `--payload=x=y`, `--payload=`).
verdicts.note: All exit 0: `--payload=-x --secret s` -> `{'data': '-x'}`; `--payload=x=y --secret s` -> `{'data': 'x=y'}` (split at first '=' only); `--payload= --secret=` -> `{'data': ''}`; `--payload=-- --secret s` -> `{'data': '--'}`. Minor overstatement in the last clause: it is not the ONLY way to pass an option-looking string — a separate token also works if it contains U+0020 (`--payload '-x y'`) or matches the negative-number regex (`--payload -1`).

verdicts.rule: Line 2 is the Python repr of the claims dict: single quotes normally, double quotes if the value contains ' and no "; non-ASCII emitted raw UTF-8.
verdicts.note: `--payload "it's" --secret s` -> `{'data': "it's"}`; `--payload 'a"b'` -> `{'data': 'a"b'}`; both quote types present -> single quotes with backslash escape: `--payload 'a'\''b"c'` -> `{'data': 'a\'b"c'}`; control chars are escaped: a literal TAB in the payload prints `{'data': 'a\tb'}`; backslashes doubled; `--payload 'héllo→'` -> `{'data': 'héllo→'}` raw UTF-8; `--payload -١` -> cat -A shows `{'data': '-M-YM-!'}` i.e. raw U+0661 bytes.
